detail.abstract: This study evaluates the effects of sugar-sweetened beverage (SSB) taxes and added sugar labeling on the purchasing behavior of carbonated soft drinks (CSD), a major contributor to excessive sugar intake. This study examines SSB taxes in Philadelphia (1.5 cents per ounce), Seattle (1.75 cents per ounce), and San Francisco (1 cent per ounce), using NielsenIQ Consumer Panel data from 2014 to 2020. Employing the generalized synthetic control method, the analysis provides robust empirical evidence while accounting for time-varying unobserved factors. The estimated effects are heterogeneous across the jurisdictions, with only Philadelphia demonstrating the anticipated negative impact on CSD purchases, which weakens over time. This finding is likely due to Philadelphia's higher average pre-tax purchases of CSD, as well as its higher tax rate and pass-through rates. Additionally, Philadelphia has a larger proportion of low-income households, which may be more sensitive to price changes. Based on the estimated effects in 2020, coinciding with the nationwide implementation of added sugar labeling, this study finds no significant effects from the combined policy measures of SSB taxes and the labeling. The findings underscore the importance of context-specific considerations when designing and implementing such policies and the potential need for complementary strategies to enhance the efficacy of SSB taxes and labeling in improving public health.

AI.tldr: 本研究评估了含糖饮料税和添加糖标签对碳酸软饮料购买行为的影响。研究发现税收效果因地区而异，只有费城显示出预期的负向影响，但这种影响随时间减弱。添加糖标签与税收的组合政策没有显著效果。

AI.method: 使用2014-2020年NielsenIQ消费者面板数据，采用广义合成控制方法分析费城、西雅图和旧金山三个城市的含糖饮料税政策效果。

detail.abstract: In this contribution, we discuss how to handle financial and sustainable investment goals, focusing on greenness and ESG features. Sustainable investing has attracted increasing interest with an associated growing commitment to take an active part in investment choices. Among thematic investments, green and energy-related ones have emerged, capturing investors' attention. Non-optimized strategies and traditional portfolio allocation models cannot guarantee the necessary flexibility. To answer this demand, ESG tailored-made allocations should be provided, with the aim of representing the preferences and commitments of investors adequately. This contribution introduces a novel ESG-focused tracking error model to optimize portfolio allocation. We consider two reference benchmarks, accounting for a financial target and an ESG one, respectively. The objective function results in a convex linear combination of the two goals where the parameter λ accounts for the investor's financial and ESG preferences. A symmetric tracking error measure is proposed to replicate the financial benchmark passively, while an asymmetric measure is used to track and possibly outperform the thematic ESG benchmark. Identifying the benchmarks for the two components represents a crucial step and, jointly with the choice of the parameter λ, accounts for the portfolio's overall risk-return and ESG profiles. In the model, the sustainability feature is handled not only with the presence of the ESG benchmark but also with the introduction of dedicated constraints. Namely, a desired minimum level of greenness and a maximum amount of carbon intensity can be accounted for. An application to the EUROSTOXX 600 equity market is presented and discussed for different choices of the parameter λ, representing different sustainability preferences and risk-return profiles. Furthermore, a discussion on the choice of the benchmarks is provided.

detail.abstract: In the large class of robust optimization methods, stochastic programming and stochastic optimization gained popularity thanks to the theoretical guarantees of the algorithms. This paper focuses on simulated annealing, a stochastic-based algorithm for numerical optimization problems with a good global exploration ability. However, the global optimum values cannot always be guaranteed without a slowly decreasing cooling schedule. This ultimately negatively impacts the convergence speed of the algorithm. This deficiency is overcome in this study by a new stochastic optimization algorithm built on generalized Metropolis and simulated annealing (SA) algorithms. The ergodicity of the proposed constrained multiple-try Metropolis SA is proved. Several constrained optimization benchmarks and challenging real-world high-dimensional problems from finance were considered for assessing the performance of the proposed algorithm.

title: The Indian Olympic Game Model: Lessons from Global Precedents for a 2036 Bid

detail.title: The Indian Olympic Game Model: Lessons from Global Precedents for a 2036 Bid
detail.abstract: As the Indian Olympic Association submitted a letter of intent to the International Olympic Committee to bid for the 2036 Summer Olympic Games, recognising the absence of an established national framework to assess its feasibility and developmental implications, this study aimed to evaluate whether hosting the Olympics can stimulate sustainable national development. The research employed a qualitative, comparative case-study approach by examining historical precedents from previous host nations, using official documents from the International Olympic Committee, academic literature, independent indices, and media analyses to evaluate four interrelated dimensions of infrastructure and urban transformation; economic growth and employment; diplomatic capital and global branding; and sports culture and legacy building. The results suggested that while the Olympics can deliver substantial benefits in terms of international visibility, urban renewal, and youth engagement, such outcomes are not automatic and depend heavily on governance capacity, fiscal discipline, and long-term legacy planning. Thereafter, this paper proposes an "Indian Olympic Games Model" emphasising a multi-city hosting framework, public-private investment synergies, and sustainability-led infrastructure design. Ultimately, the study highlights that India's Olympic aspiration represents both a transformative opportunity and a structural challenge, contingent upon evidence-based planning and institutional coordination.

detail.title: A Valuation Model and Trading Strategy for U.S. Agency MBSs

declarations.funderStatement: This study was supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number JP23K04285.

detail.abstract: A mortgage-backed security (MBS) is a securitized instrument whose cash flows consist of principal and interest payments from an underlying pool of residential mortgage loans. Compared to government and corporate bonds, MBS exhibits more complex cash flow structures due to embedded prepayment options. This paper examines the TBA (To-Be-Announced) market, a highly liquid forward market for U.S. agency MBSs, and investigates whether persistent mispricing exists from which investors can benefit. To this end, we construct a trading strategy based on an arbitrage-free model. We adopt a no-arbitrage pricing framework as the MBS valuation model, incorporating four latent factors that jointly capture interest rate risk, credit risk, and prepayment risk. The model is estimated using observable data such as TBA forward prices. Empirical analysis reveals that the price difference between observed TBA market prices and theoretical prices exhibits meanreverting behavior over time. Furthermore, the price difference exhibits an inverse smile shape with respect to moneyness, defined as the fixed mortgage rate of each MBS minus the current mortgage rate. TBA contracts near the at-the-money level tend to be overvalued, whereas those further away tend to be undervalued. An arbitrage trading strategy that uses this price discrepancy as a mispricing signal earns an average annualized excess return of 58.27 bps relative to an equally weighted benchmark portfolio. The time-series behavior of excess returns reveals distinct periods of strong outperformance and periods of limited gains.

AI.tldr: 该论文研究了美国机构抵押贷款支持证券（MBS）的TBA市场，发现存在持续的定价偏差。通过构建基于无套利定价模型的交易策略，发现TBA市场价格与理论价格之间存在均值回归行为，且价格差异呈现反向微笑形状。利用这种定价偏差的交易策略可获得58.27基点的年化超额收益。
AI.research_question: 美国机构MBS的TBA市场中是否存在持续的定价偏差，投资者能否从中获利？
AI.motivation: 与政府和公司债券相比，MBS具有更复杂的现金流结构，特别是内含提前还款期权。TBA市场作为高度流动的远期市场，其定价效率值得研究。
AI.theoretical_framework: 无套利定价框架，包含四个潜在因子：利率风险、信用风险和提前还款风险。
AI.method: 采用无套利定价模型作为MBS估值模型，使用TBA远期价格等可观测数据进行模型估计，构建基于定价偏差的交易策略。
AI.findings: TBA市场价格与理论价格差异呈现均值回归行为；价格差异相对于货币性呈现反向微笑形状；平价附近的TBA合约倾向于被高估，而远离平价的合约倾向于被低估。
AI.theory_contributions: 为MBS定价提供了包含多重风险因子的无套利框架，揭示了TBA市场的定价偏差模式。
AI.practical_contributions: 开发了基于定价偏差的交易策略，可获得显著的超额收益，为投资者提供了套利机会。

title: Agricultural Robotics and the Fourth Agricultural Revolution: Innovation, Industry Dynamics, and the Equity-Efficiency Paradox

detail.title: Agricultural Robotics and the Fourth Agricultural Revolution: Innovation, Industry Dynamics, and the Equity-Efficiency Paradox

declarations.ethicsApproval: No interviews, no experiments.

detail.abstract: Agricultural robotics represents a cornerstone technology of the Fourth Agricultural Revolution, promising significant environmental benefits through precision operations while addressing critical labor shortages. This paper examines agricultural robotics through multiple lenses: technological innovation, environmental sustainability, industry structure, geopolitical competition, and social equity. Drawing on innovation diffusion theory and empirical evidence from industry data and farmer interviews, we analyze how robotic systems reduce herbicide usage by 50-90%, improve harvest efficiency, and optimize resource allocation. However, we identify a fundamental "equity-efficiency paradox": technologies delivering the greatest environmental and productivity gains often impose the most severe social costs, including labor displacement, mental health impacts, technological lock-in, and concentration of economic benefits among large-scale operators and multinational corporations. The paper maps the geopolitical dimensions of agricultural robotics, examining how US-China-EU competition shapes technology development, and analyzes market concentration trends that favor incumbent equipment manufacturers. We conclude by identifying critical research questions around just transition pathways, welfare modeling of distributional impacts, and governance mechanisms to ensure that agricultural automation serves broad societal goals rather than primarily enriching technology providers at the expense of farm workers and smallholder farmers.

detail.abstract: This policy brief examines the implementation of the Ecology-Based Neighborhood Budget Allocation (ALAKE), an ecological budget tagging model initiated by the City of Singkawang, Indonesia. ALAKE adapts the Ecological Fiscal Transfer (EFT) framework to incorporate environmental performance indicators into local budgeting processes. Using a qualitative and participatory approach, the study identifies ecological and social indicators that guide expenditure alignment. The results show that environmental tagging enhances planning coherence, citizen participation, and environmentally responsive budgeting. This policy brief provides actionable insights for strengthening local governance and aligning fiscal policy with Indonesia’s sustainable and low-carbon development goals.

title: Developing A Strategic Framework to Enhance Lebanon's Tourism Sector with the Goal of Creating Sustainable Employment Opportunities through Targeted Marketing Initiatives

detail.title: Developing A Strategic Framework to Enhance Lebanon's Tourism Sector with the Goal of Creating Sustainable Employment Opportunities through Targeted Marketing Initiatives
detail.abstract:
Lebanon’s tourism sector has faced major setbacks from the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut port explosion, and economic collapse, leading to unemployment and reduced investment.

Despite these challenges, Lebanon’s cultural heritage and natural assets offer strong recovery potentials.

This study develops a strategic framework to enhance the tourism sector and create sustainable employment through targeted marketing initiatives.

Using a multi-method qualitative approach, it analyzes interviews and former studies to explore how cultural routes, particularly the Phoenician Route, can boost tourism and induce job creation.

Findings disclose that an adaptive marketing mix and stakeholder collaboration can strengthen Lebanon’s global image, attract investment, and support community-based tourism.

The study subsidizes practical strategies for policymakers to achieve sustainable tourism and economic resilience in post-crisis thriving Lebanon.

detail.title: When LLMs Hurt More than Help: Understanding Decision Failures Under AI Assistance

publicationDetails.detailsText: NYU Stern School of Business Research Paper Forthcoming
publicationDetails.journalName: New York University Stern School of Business Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded into high-stakes decision workflows across domains such as finance, hiring, and admissions, yet their impact on human judgment remains poorly understood. Many of these organizations now rely on hybrid workflows where machine learning models flag uncertain cases for human review. These borderline decisions—where predictive confidence is low—are precisely where LLM assistance may be helpful for human reviewers. We study how LLMs influence human judgment in such contexts through a controlled behavioral experiment involving around 1,000 participants making binary income classification decisions.  We examine two types of LLM support interventions: an LLM-generated summary and an interactive LLM decision support chat tool. While summaries provide informationally equivalent descriptions of profiles, the chat tool enables open-ended data queries on the training data in natural language. We find LLM summaries do not affect decision responses or decision quality. On the other hand, the chat tool does not improve accuracy, but systematically alters decision patterns. Specifically, interaction with an LLM chat increases confidence without corresponding accuracy gains and re-allocates errors across the decision boundary. Textual analyses of chat transcripts reveal that participants anchor on statistical summaries and interpret neutral information as normative, reducing analytical engagement. Our results highlight that even “neutral” LLM tools can amplify cognitive biases. These findings offer new behavioral insights into human–AI collaboration and underscore the need for decision support systems designed for calibration, not persuasion.

AI.tldr: 本研究通过行为实验发现，在边界决策中，LLM生成的摘要不影响人类判断，但交互式LLM聊天工具会系统性地改变决策模式——增加信心却不提高准确性，并重新分配错误。这表明即使是"中立"的AI工具也会放大认知偏见。
AI.research_question: LLM如何影响人类在边界决策中的判断？
AI.motivation: LLM越来越多地嵌入金融、招聘和招生等高风险决策流程，但其对人类判断的影响尚不清楚。在机器学习模型标记不确定案例供人工审查的混合工作流中，LLM辅助可能特别有用。
AI.theoretical_framework: 人类-AI协作、认知偏见、决策支持系统、锚定效应
AI.method: 对约1,000名参与者进行受控行为实验，涉及二元收入分类决策。比较两种LLM支持干预：LLM生成的摘要和交互式LLM决策支持聊天工具。
AI.findings: LLM摘要不影响决策响应或质量；聊天工具不提高准确性，但系统性地改变决策模式——增加信心而不提高准确性，重新分配决策边界错误；参与者锚定统计摘要，将中性信息解释为规范性，减少分析参与度。
AI.theory_contributions: 为人类-AI协作提供新的行为洞察；证明即使是"中立"的LLM工具也会放大认知偏见；强调决策支持系统需要为校准而非说服而设计。
AI.practical_contributions: 提醒组织在部署LLM决策支持工具时需谨慎；强调需要设计能够校准而非放大偏见的系统；为高风险决策环境中的AI工具设计提供指导。

title: Closing the Data Gap: Rethinking Measurement Infrastructure for Public Sector Progress on the SDGs
affiliations: Stanford University

detail.title: Closing the Data Gap: Rethinking Measurement Infrastructure for Public Sector Progress on the SDGs
detail.abstract: Weak, non-comparable SDG metrics impede progress in health, well-being, and education and invite politicization of otherwise technical objectives. First, we show that effective public human resource management (HRM)-including strategic workforce planning, performance management, and capacity development-depends on clear, credible data for decision-making and evaluation. Second, we use the Gallup World Poll and the Global Flourishing Study as illustrative global infrastructures for SDG-aligned measurement, particularly for "soft" outcomes such as life satisfaction, perceived safety, institutional trust, and employment quality that cut across multiple goals. Leveraging these harmonized survey platforms can close core monitoring gaps and support distribution-sensitive assessment, but doing so requires modernization and interoperability of international statistical systems. Strengthening global data architectures is therefore not a technical afterthought; it is foundational for policy learning, program accountability, and depoliticized progress reporting.

AI.tldr: 本文论证了强化全球数据架构对于实现可持续发展目标的重要性，特别是通过改进公共人力资源管理，并利用盖洛普世界民意调查和全球繁荣研究等全球调查基础设施来测量软性成果，以填补监测空白并支持政策学习和问责。
AI.research_question: 如何通过加强全球数据架构和利用全球调查基础设施来改进可持续发展目标的测量和实现？
AI.motivation: 当前可持续发展目标的指标薄弱且不可比较，阻碍了健康、福祉和教育领域的进展，并导致技术性目标被政治化。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于公共人力资源管理理论和全球数据治理理论，强调清晰可信的数据对决策和评估的重要性。
AI.method: 使用盖洛普世界民意调查和全球繁荣研究作为说明性案例，分析全球调查基础设施在测量软性成果方面的潜力。
AI.findings: 有效的公共人力资源管理依赖于清晰可信的数据，全球调查基础设施可以填补核心监测空白并支持分布敏感评估。
AI.theory_contributions: 提出了将全球数据架构建设作为政策学习和问责基础的理论框架，强调了数据现代化和互操作性的重要性。
AI.practical_contributions: 为政策制定者提供了利用现有全球调查平台改进SDG测量的具体路径，强调了加强国际统计系统现代化的必要性。

title: Verifiable Cleanliness for LLMs: A Baseline Framework for Supply-Chain Auditability and Poison Resistance
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Verifiable Cleanliness for LLMs: A Baseline Framework for Supply-Chain Auditability and Poison Resistance
detail.abstract: Small-budget training-data poisoning makes open LLM pipelines a governance problem, not just a technical one. This paper introduces a practical baseline: a machine-readable Data-SBOM (DSBOM), an operational CAP protocol (Cleanliness–Audit–Provenance), and a reproducible pre-deployment Poison Stress Test (PST), plus metrics (TIGI, R-Persist, S-Frag, A-Score) to measure susceptibility and auditability. Together these artifacts form a testable gate and deployment roadmap for enterprises, model hubs, and regulators to raise provable cleanliness and reduce poisoning risk.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了一个针对开放LLM管道数据投毒问题的治理框架，包括机器可读的数据SBOM、CAP协议、毒化压力测试及相关度量指标，为企业、模型中心和监管机构提供可测试的门控和部署路线图。
AI.research_question: 如何有效治理开放LLM管道中的数据投毒风险？
AI.motivation: 小预算训练数据投毒使开放LLM管道成为治理问题而不仅仅是技术问题，需要建立可证明的清洁度和降低投毒风险的机制。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于数据供应链管理和安全治理理论，构建机器可读的数据SBOM框架和CAP协议。
AI.method: 提出操作性CAP协议（清洁度-审计-溯源）、可重现的预部署毒化压力测试（PST）以及相关度量指标（TIGI、R-Persist、S-Frag、A-Score）。
AI.findings: 这些工具共同形成了可测试的门控和部署路线图，能够提高可证明的清洁度并降低投毒风险。
AI.theory_contributions: 将数据投毒问题从技术问题提升为治理问题，建立了机器可读的数据SBOM理论框架。
AI.practical_contributions: 为企业、模型中心和监管机构提供了具体的操作协议、测试方法和度量指标，便于实际应用和监管。

title: A Generation at Risk? Creativity, PISA 2022, and the Demands of an AI Economy and Society in 2025
affiliations: Narxoz University

detail.title: A Generation at Risk? Creativity, PISA 2022, and the Demands of an AI Economy and Society in 2025
detail.abstract: Debates on the future of work emphasize creativity as a key skill, yet education systems often fail to deliver it at scale. Drawing on PISA 2022 data, we construct cross-domain indices to compare creativity outcomes with mathematics, reading, and science. Results show creativity scores are not only lower but also more widely dispersed across countries, highlighting a gap between policy rhetoric and classroom reality. In 2025, this gap is especially urgent: rapid AI growth coincides with the 2022 PISA cohort (now 18-19 years old) entering university and the workforce. Our analysis suggests most education systems are underprepared. We conclude by outlining practical steps for embedding creativity into curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment.

AI.tldr: 基于PISA 2022数据构建跨领域创造力指数，发现创造力得分不仅低于数学、阅读和科学，而且在各国间差异更大，揭示了政策口号与课堂现实之间的差距。随着AI快速发展，这一差距在2025年尤为紧迫。
AI.research_question: 教育系统在创造力培养方面存在哪些差距？如何比较创造力与数学、阅读、科学等传统学科的表现？
AI.motivation: 关于未来工作的讨论强调创造力是关键技能，但教育系统往往无法大规模培养创造力。随着AI快速发展，2022年PISA队列（现18-19岁）即将进入大学和职场，这一差距尤为紧迫。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于PISA评估框架，构建跨领域创造力指数，比较创造力与传统学科的表现差异。
AI.method: 使用PISA 2022数据，构建跨领域创造力指数，并与数学、阅读、科学成绩进行比较分析。
AI.findings: 创造力得分不仅低于数学、阅读和科学，而且在各国间分布更分散，表明大多数教育系统在创造力培养方面准备不足。
AI.theory_contributions: 提供了创造力与传统学科表现的实证比较，揭示了教育系统在创造力培养方面的系统性差距。
AI.practical_contributions: 为将创造力融入课程、教学和评估提供了实践步骤，帮助教育系统应对AI时代对创造性人才的需求。

title: From Labour to Longevity: A Panel Study of Health and Employment Drivers of Female Life Expectancy in LMICs
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Labour to Longevity: A Panel Study of Health and Employment Drivers of Female Life Expectancy in LMICs
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the health and labour market determinants of female life expectancy across 96 Low-and-Middle-Income Countries (LMICs) over the years 2000, 2010 and 2019. By combining labour market indicators with key health variables, this paper provides an in-depth analysis of the factors influencing female life expectancy in resource-constrained contexts. By using panel data from the World Bank's World Development Indicators and employing a fixed effects regression model, this paper isolates within-country variations while controlling for unobserved heterogeneity. It was observed that fertility rates and HIV prevalence are the most statistically significant negative predictors of female life expectancy, indicating the need for reproductive autonomy and disease prevention. Female unemployment did not display a statistically significant coefficient in the fixed-effects model, and employment in agriculture and vulnerable employment were statistically significant and negative, while the wage-and-salaried share was also statistically significant but negative due to severe collinearity with vulnerable employment. Robustness checks supported the analysis: the Hausman test confirmed that fixed effects was the appropriate model choice, while variance inflation factor (VIF) results helped address multicollinearity concerns. These findings display the need for gender-sensitive public health and labour policies in LMICs, including better access to family planning, HIV interventions, and formalization of femaledominated employment sectors. This paper expands upon the growing interdisciplinary literature on gender and development by empirically demonstrating how economic and health structures together shape female life expectancy in the developing world.

AI.tldr: 本文研究了96个中低收入国家女性预期寿命的健康和劳动力市场决定因素，发现生育率和HIV流行率是最显著的负面预测因子，而女性失业率不显著，农业就业和脆弱就业对女性预期寿命有负面影响。
AI.research_question: 中低收入国家女性预期寿命的健康和劳动力市场决定因素是什么？
AI.motivation: 在资源受限的环境中，结合劳动力市场指标和健康变量，深入分析影响女性预期寿命的因素，为性别敏感政策提供实证依据。
AI.theoretical_framework: 性别与发展交叉学科理论，关注经济结构和健康系统如何共同塑造发展中国家的女性预期寿命。
AI.method: 使用世界银行世界发展指标的面板数据，采用固定效应回归模型，控制不可观测的异质性，分析2000、2010和2019年的数据。
AI.findings: 生育率和HIV流行率是最显著的负面预测因子；女性失业率不显著；农业就业和脆弱就业显著负面；工资和薪金份额因与脆弱就业严重共线性而显示为负。
AI.theory_contributions: 扩展了性别与发展的跨学科文献，实证展示了经济和健康结构如何共同影响发展中国家女性预期寿命。
AI.practical_contributions: 为中低收入国家制定性别敏感的公共卫生和劳动力政策提供依据，包括改善计划生育服务、HIV干预措施以及女性主导就业部门的正规化。

title: Reimagining ODL Instructional Approaches in Preparing Open Secondary School Students in Malawi for Evolving Global Market
affiliations: , Nalikule College of Education, Nalikule College of Education, Nalikule College of Education and Nalikule College of Education

detail.title: Reimagining ODL Instructional Approaches in Preparing Open Secondary School Students in Malawi for Evolving Global Market
detail.abstract: This paper investigated the effectiveness of Open distance and e-learning (ODeL) instruction in Malawi's Open Secondary School (OSS). Employing Technology, Pedagogy and Content Knowledge framework and concurrent mixed methods, the study sampled six OSS, involving 6 head teachers, 6 ODeL coordinators and 24 teachers. Differentiated instruction is credited for enhancing student's motivation, performance, and self-efficacy. However, findings indicated over-reliance of teacher-centered methods. Eighty-six percent of coordinators and 72% of teachers attached this to overcrowded classes and limited contact time. The study underscored the necessity to integrate technology into differentiated instructions to address these constraints. In response to the challenges, Competence and Material in Differentiated Instruction framework was developed to advance use of technology in differentiated instruction. It is envisaged that the developed instructional framework would revolutionize the existing OSS instructional practices in open schools. This initiative aligns with Regional ODL Strategic Plan 2022–2030 and Malawi Vision 2063, promoting inclusive, self-reliant national development through effective education reform.

AI.tldr: 本研究调查了马拉维开放中学(ODeL)远程教学的成效，发现差异化教学能提升学生动机和表现，但存在过度依赖教师中心方法的问题，主要原因是班级拥挤和接触时间有限。研究开发了CMD框架来整合技术于差异化教学中。
AI.research_question: 马拉维开放中学的远程教学效果如何？
AI.motivation: 评估马拉维开放中学远程教学的有效性，为教育改进提供依据
AI.theoretical_framework: 技术、教学法和内容知识框架(TPACK)
AI.method: 并行混合方法研究，抽样6所开放中学，涉及6名校长、6名协调员和24名教师
AI.findings: 差异化教学能提升学生动机、表现和自我效能；但存在过度依赖教师中心方法的问题；86%协调员和72%教师将此归因于班级拥挤和有限接触时间
AI.theory_contributions: 开发了CMD(能力与材料差异化教学)框架，推进技术在差异化教学中的应用
AI.practical_contributions: 为马拉维开放中学提供改进教学实践的框架，支持区域远程教育战略和马拉维2063愿景

title: ZulfiQode: A Computational Approach to Systematic Theme Mining of Financial Ethics
affiliations: , University of Engineering & Technology (Taxila), University of Engineering & Technology (Taxila), National Defence University and Office of the Prime Minister

detail.title: ZulfiQode: A Computational Approach to Systematic Theme Mining of Financial Ethics
detail.abstract: This paper introduces ZulfiQode, a computational framework for thematic mining in financial ethics. The approach fuses Natural Language Processing (NLP) with a structured back-end architecture to enable efficient text analysis. It extracts recurring behavioral themes using a dynamic codebook generated via TF-IDF weighting. The system prioritizes patterns based on relative prominence and recurrence. ZulfiQode processes narrative-driven content such as investor transcripts. It identifies ethical signals, persuasive tactics, and anomalies in reasoning. Semantic classification occurs through automated matching and hierarchical grouping, minimizing human intervention and bias. We apply this methodology to dialogues by Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger. These conversations reveal consistent themes: skepticism, manipulative projection, trust filtering, and institutional negligence. The system detects such motifs with accuracy and repeatability. The modular and scalable design makes ZulfiQode adaptable to domains beyond finance, such as legal reviews, corporate disclosures, and policy evaluations. Its pivotal advantage lies in the structured automation of qualitative insight. In conclusion, this work underscores the significant potential of computational systems in decoding ethical behavior. ZulfiQode offers a clear, dynamic, and extensible pathway for researchers exploring integrity in decision-driven narratives.

AI.tldr: ZulfiQode是一个用于金融伦理主题挖掘的计算框架，融合NLP和结构化后端架构，通过TF-IDF加权生成动态代码本提取行为主题，应用于巴菲特和芒格的对话分析，识别出怀疑主义、操纵性投射、信任过滤和制度疏忽等伦理模式。
AI.research_question: 如何通过计算框架自动挖掘金融伦理中的主题模式？
AI.motivation: 传统定性分析存在主观性和效率问题，需要自动化工具来系统性地识别伦理行为模式。
AI.theoretical_framework: 自然语言处理、主题建模、TF-IDF加权、语义分类、伦理行为理论。
AI.method: 融合NLP与结构化后端架构，使用TF-IDF生成动态代码本，通过自动匹配和层次分组进行语义分类，分析投资者对话等叙述性内容。
AI.findings: 在巴菲特和芒格的对话中识别出四个一致主题：怀疑主义、操纵性投射、信任过滤和制度疏忽，系统具有高准确性和可重复性。
AI.theory_contributions: 提出了一个计算伦理分析的理论框架，将定性伦理洞察结构化自动化。
AI.practical_contributions: 开发了可扩展的ZulfiQode系统，适用于金融、法律、企业披露和政策评估等多个领域，提高了伦理分析的效率和客观性。

title: The Ragsdale Framework for Autonomous Organizations: The Work CPU
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Ragsdale Framework for Autonomous Organizations: The Work CPU

declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted without external funding or institutional sponsorship. It represents the independent scholarly work of Marc Ragsdale and is not commissioned, financed, or owned by Kaamfu Inc. or any affiliated organization. While Kaamfu applies elements of the Framework in practice, the Framework itself is authored and maintained independently, and all rights to its theoretical development remain with the author.

detail.abstract:
This paper formalizes the Work CPU as an individual-level processing model that standardizes how work enters, moves, and exits the domain of a worker or agent. The model defines two primitives: the Demand Queue for capturing inbound requests, instructions, and signals, and the Activity Queue for recording work in motion and delivered outputs. Together, these queues provide live status, role-based visibility, and universal traceability.
The Work CPU extends beyond metaphor to structural architecture, drawing direct parallels with computing principles such as instruction sets, pipelines, scheduling, parallelism, and error handling. It specifies a minimal instruction set, pipeline stages, rights and visibility models, error-handling rules, and performance metrics including throughput, latency, workload balance, and a measurable concept of management parallelism.

Positioned within the Prerequisite System of the Ragsdale Framework for Autonomous Organizations (RFAO), the Work CPU provides the substrate of execution on which alignment, acceleration, and autonomization depend. A review of partial precedents highlights why no existing tool delivers a true processor at the individual level. Looking forward, the paper argues that interoperability among competing Work CPUs is essential to avoid fragmentation, and envisions a future in which every human and every artificial agent functions as a Work CPU, operating within shared principles that allow work to flow seamlessly across organizations and ecosystems.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了Work CPU模型，将个体工作者标准化为处理工作请求的处理器架构，包含需求队列和活动队列两个核心组件，并借鉴计算原理定义了指令集、流水线、调度等机制。
AI.research_question: 如何建立一个标准化的个体工作处理模型，实现工作流程的可视化、可追踪和互操作性？
AI.motivation: 现有工具缺乏真正的个体级处理器模型，无法提供统一的工作流程标准化和跨组织互操作性。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于计算原理（指令集、流水线、调度、并行性、错误处理）和Ragsdale自主组织框架的先决系统理论。
AI.method: 概念模型构建，通过定义需求队列和活动队列两个基本原语，以及最小指令集、流水线阶段、权限模型等组件。
AI.findings: Work CPU模型能够提供实时状态、基于角色的可见性和通用可追溯性，为组织对齐、加速和自主化提供执行基础。
AI.theory_contributions: 将计算处理器概念扩展到个体工作处理领域，建立了标准化的个体工作处理架构理论。
AI.practical_contributions: 为组织提供了可实施的工作流程标准化方案，支持跨组织工作流互操作，并为未来人机协作提供了统一框架。

title: Executive Presence Reimagined: The CORE Presence Model for Leading with Authenticity, Confidence, and Emotional Intelligence- Elevating Leadership through Identity, Emotional Mastery, and Regulation
affiliations: Harvard University

detail.title: Executive Presence Reimagined: The CORE Presence Model for Leading with Authenticity, Confidence, and Emotional Intelligence- Elevating Leadership through Identity, Emotional Mastery, and Regulation

declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: Self

detail.abstract: Executive presence is widely recognized as a crucial factor for career advancement and leadership effectiveness, yet it remains ambiguously defined and often misunderstood. Traditionally associated with surface-level traits such as poise, articulation, and professional demeanour, executive presence is frequently cultivated through performance-based approaches. However, these strategies overlook the substantial influence of internal psychological conditions-particularly social anxiety, imposter syndrome, and perfectionism-that silently obstruct the emergence of authentic leadership. This paper challenges the prevailing paradigm by reframing executive presence as an outcome of cognitive-emotional alignment rather than mere behavioral refinement. It critically examines the intersection between executive presence and psychological barriers, emphasizing that the ability to "show up" powerfully in leadership contexts requires inner stability, self-awareness, and regulated emotional expression. Through a comprehensive review of interdisciplinary literature and thematic synthesis of organizational behavior, neuroscience, and leadership psychology, the paper introduces an original and academically grounded framework: the CORE Presence Model-Cognition, Ownership, Regulation, and Expression. The model proposes a four-pillar approach to cultivating executive presence from the inside out. It targets maladaptive thought patterns, strengthens leadership identity, enhances emotional regulation, and aligns expressive behavior with internal clarity. Unlike traditional skill-based models, the CORE Presence Model provides a psychologically sustainable and inclusive roadmap for individuals and organizations to develop leadership presence, particularly in high-stakes and psychologically demanding environments. By integrating psychological resilience with leadership capability, the paper offers new insights into how executive presence can be nurtured authentically-even among individuals historically marginalized by conventional norms of leadership visibility. It positions the development of executive presence not merely as a personal endeavor, but as a strategic imperative for organizations committed to inclusion, mental wellness, and authentic leadership pipelines.

AI.tldr: 本文挑战了将高管形象视为表面行为特质的传统观点，提出了CORE Presence Model（认知、所有权、调节、表达），强调高管形象是认知情绪对齐的结果，需要从内部心理条件入手培养。
AI.research_question: 高管形象如何受到内部心理障碍（如社交焦虑、冒名顶替综合症、完美主义）的影响，以及如何通过心理层面的干预来培养真实的高管形象？

detail.abstract: The construction industry is one of the most labour-intensive sectors in the world. But There is a pervasive and ongoing pattern of human rights abuses of Construction workers. These workers frequently face dangerous working conditions, wage exploitation, discrimination, and the denial of basic social safeguards, especially those in contract, informal, or migratory positions. Through the prism of fundamental ILO treaties, international human rights legislation, and pertinent state legal frameworks, this essay critically investigates these infractions. In accordance with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) and the International Covenant on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights (ICESCR), the study starts by placing the right to work, fair and favorable working circumstances, and occupational safety in the framework of fundamental human rights. It examines the frequency of child labor, forced labor, and unfair hiring practices, especially in international construction projects where migrant workers are at risk of identity document seizure and debt bondage. In addition, gender-specific issues that worsen women's marginalization in the construction industry are discussed, including sexual harassment, lack of maternity protection, and salary inequity. The research assesses the efficacy of statutory protections, including welfare board programs, compensation legislation, and occupational health and safety standards. by comparing the legal systems of India, the United Kingdom, and the United States. It also looks at the drawbacks of the program, such as the exclusion of informal workers from social security coverage, insufficient grievance redressal procedures, and weak enforcement measures. Under the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, the function of trade unions, collective bargaining, and corporate accountability is evaluated as a means of prevention and remediation. In the paper's conclusion, a multifaceted strategy that incorporates rights-based business due diligence, strict enforcement, inclusive welfare measures, and stronger legislative protections is recommended. To protect the dignity, health, and livelihoods of construction workers around the world, this research emphasizes the urgent need for concerted legislative and policy reforms by framing labor rights as human rights.

detail.abstract: Businesses in all sectors, including most downstream segments, depend on biodiversity and the ecosystem services it sustains, yet firms also exert pressures that accelerate biodiversity loss. The latter generates material risks for both companies and their financial stakeholders. Mapping corporate dependencies and impacts on nature is therefore critical to mitigating pressures and halting biodiversity decline. ENCORE (Exploring Natural Capital Opportunities, Risks and Exposure) has become a leading framework for assessing businessnature linkages. However, ENCORE primarily reflects direct operations, leading to a potential underestimation of exposures across value-chains and systemic risk to both nature and businesses. This paper reviews institutional uses of ENCORE, analyses methodological constraints related to value-chain integration, and introduces an approach to extend ENCORE's utility and highlight exposures across value-chains. By making such previously hidden exposures visible, our approach extends ENCORE's utility and enables more in-depth double materiality assessments, risk management, and alignment with evolving regulatory expectations.

detail.abstract: Hurricanes cause significant wind and water damage, yet economic research primarily focuses on the latter due to data limitations. We overcome this problem by analyzing photographs taken after Hurricane Irma (2017) to locate blue-tarped homes. Using a regression discontinuity framework, we find the 2001 Florida Building Code impacted wind risk for over 500,000 homeowners. Adopters were 22% less likely to experience wind damage and saw a 27% reduction in damage severity. Unrepaired properties also sold for 13.3% ($29,400) less and were harder to sell, underscoring the importance of building codes in mitigating risk and promoting climate change adaptation.

detail.abstract: How do people at the extremes of local socioeconomic status (Bay Area residents experiencing homelessness and affluent residents) use social ties to move economically? This pilot case study pairs short egocentric network interviews with qualitative modules to trace the places and routines that seed relationships, and the mechanisms that turn encounters into help or harm. The analysis builds on Granovetter's embeddedness framework and work on weak ties. Across five interviews, I find two patterns: in survival settings, safety and loss set the stage for tie churn, with aid often arriving through family or chance, and with theft and document loss blocking access to formal brokers; in affluent settings, trust, competence, investment help, or housing opportunities. Cross-class ties surface in professional contexts (e.g., doctor-patient) and in mixed social gatherings, but their durability depends on trust and repeated contact rather than a single meeting. I close with design implications for shelters and elite organizations that want to widen pathways for inclusive brokerage without tokenism, and I outline a larger study that scales this pilot.

detail.abstract: This paper provides causal evidence that the sex composition of dating markets affects maternal and neonatal health. Using a novel instrument that leverages randomness in sex at birth to vary the availability of male partners, I find that a more favorable dating market for women decreases non-marital but increases marital fertility, lowers rates of chlamydia and hypertension among mothers, and decreases the incidence of low APGAR scores and a composite index of adverse birth outcomes. Connecting this to inequalities, racial disparities in partner availability can explain 5–10% of the Black–White pregnancy health gap.

title: Seeing is Believing: The Role of Visual-Verbal Congruence in Crowdfunding Disclosures

detail.title: Seeing is Believing: The Role of Visual-Verbal Congruence in Crowdfunding Disclosures
detail.abstract: Prior research in accounting has focused extensively on the role of disclosure quality and information transparency in reducing information asymmetry and the cost of capital. However, only a limited set of prior work examines the increasingly important feature of imagery in firm disclosures. In addition, the voluminous content of annual reports makes it difficult to cleanly identify the effect of the images themselves in the context of the tens of thousands of words contained in a typical report (much less the impact of images in voluntary firm disclosures on the internet or elsewhere). With the advent of LLMs, it is now possible to process the rich information contained in images, and we utilize this method to process a simple disclosure-investment context using Kickstarter projects. We find that congruence between information contained in the Kickstarter project image and the project description (visual-verbal congruence) leads to increased project funding and a greater probability of success for the project. We also find that this effect is stronger for project categories where visual information is intuitively more critical. Our results indicate that investors' judgments are strongly shaped by visual-verbal congruence in disclosures, and we introduce an innovative methodology for processing non-textual disclosure information.

detail.abstract: We study optimal and strategic extraction of a renewable resource that is distributed over a network, migrates mass-conservingly across nodes, and evolves under nonlinear (concave) growth. A subset of nodes hosts extractors while the remaining nodes serve as reserves. We analyze a centralized planner and a noncooperative game with stationary Markov strategies. The migration operator transports shadow values along the network so that Perron-Frobenius geometry governs long-run spatial allocations, while nonlinear growth couples aggregate biomass with its spatial distribution and bounds global dynamics. For three canonical growth families, logistic, power, and log-type saturating laws, under related unilities, we derive closed-form value functions and feedback rules for the planner and construct a symmetric Markov equilibrium on strongly connected networks. To our knowledge, this is the first paper to obtain explicit policies for spatial resource extraction with nonlinear growth and, a fortiori, closed-form Markov equilibria, on general networks.

detail.title: Export, Exchange Rate, Inflation, FDI, and Economic Growth in Bangladesh: A Time Series Analysis
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of internal and external factors on Bangladesh’s long-term economic growth, with a focus on inflation, exchange rates, foreign direct investment (FDI), and exports. Understanding these relationships is crucial for policymakers, particularly in light of the country’s ongoing economic transformations and external pressures. The research utilizes annual data from 1986 to 2022 and employs the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model to examine both short-term and long-term relationships. This model considers stationarity and cointegration among variables, ensuring reliable results. Diagnostic tests confirm the model’s dependability. The study reveals that currency depreciation has a positive impact on economic growth by enhancing export competitiveness. Although inflation has a negative but statistically insignificant effect, and FDI shows a positive but statistically insignificant influence, these results suggest a need for more effective investment policies. Exports contribute to growth in the short term, though their long-term importance is limited, emphasizing the need for export diversification. The error correction model suggests a robust adjustment process that promotes long-term economic stability. However, the study’s scope is limited by excluding key structural factors, such as labor market dynamics, technological progress, and institutional quality, which could further explain variations in growth. Additionally, using only annual data restricts the ability to capture short-term fluctuations and external shocks, such as political instability or global crises. Overall, this research adds to existing knowledge by thoroughly examining the internal and external factors affecting Bangladesh’s economic growth through a robust econometric approach. The findings offer valuable insights for policymakers in developing economies seeking to strike a balance between currency stability, controlling inflation, promoting investment-driven growth, and encouraging export diversification.

detail.abstract: Vertical restraints in labor markets are a neglected topic, but have taken on importance as the harms caused by labor market restraints have gained greater recognition. detail.title: The Impact of in-Law Mortality on Women's Labor Supply in India
detail.abstract: We examine how the death of co-residing in-laws affects married women's labor force participation in India. Dynamic difference-in-differences estimates indicate a 19 percent increase in participation following the death of a co-residing father-in-law (FIL), but no change after that of a mother-in-law (MIL). Income effects are directionally consistent in some cases but lack strong statistical support. Time use evidence shows that women living with widowed FILs spend more time on domestic work, while those with widowed MILs spend more time in employment. Both increases come at the expense of leisure and sleep. Measures of agency shift marginally: women gain financial autonomy and husbands assume greater decision-making power following FIL death, while women's own decision-making increases modestly after MIL death. These results point to the distinctive role of senior male authority, as opposed to co-residence per se, in constraining women's labor supply.

detail.abstract: The study analyses about the relationship between economic growth and carbon emission levels in Germany between 1990 till 2023. Since Germany is the biggest economy in Europe and has well-established climate policies, it serves as a unique example for checking if development is possible without damaging the environment. The study examines the question that whether German growth is causing more carbon emissions or if it has managed to decouple these two by reforming its environment. To examine this, the study uses data on GDP, carbon emissions, energy consumption, renewable energy, industrial production, the number of people in the workforce and environmental stringency index for each year. Stability of the data, correlations in the long run and short-term changes are studied using the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test, the Johansen cointegration test and the Vector Error Correction Model (VECM). Results suggest that over the long run; carbon emissions and economic growth are closely linked and show minor changes that occur daily. It also confirms that at the initial stages of economic growth CO2 emissions increase, but later decline as action is taken to cope up with). Results research expands the studies by exploring Germany’s experience over the last three decades. Policy makers can use these results to support efforts for both the economy and the environment. It appears that being environmentally friendly and following existing laws does not hurt the economy in Germany.

detail.title: Retirement Accumulation Strategies with Real Assets and Inflation Risk
detail.abstract:
This article presents a comprehensive, dynamic asset allocation framework for retirement savings, extending the classical Merton model to include human capital. This framework reconciles the intuitive age-based glide path with financial theory, recognizing that total wealth consists of financial capital and the present value of future contributions. It shows that the optimal allocation of risky assets depends on the ratio of human to financial capital, risk aversion, investment horizon, and key market parameters, such as the risk premium and volatility. Under CRRA utility, closed-form solutions are derived, demonstrating that continuous contributions increase risk exposure relative to the constant-mix strategy. The article also compares glide path strategies with constant-mix approaches, revealing that glide paths generally provide better downside protection and higher probabilities of meeting retirement goals, while dynamically adjusting risk exposure over time. The analysis further examines the shape of the glide path and shows that practical constraints, such as leverage limits, time-varying risk aversion, and rising contribution patterns, transform the theoretically convex allocation path into the empirically observed concave form.

The article expands the model to include multiple asset classes, providing a deep analysis of the practical differences between single-asset and multi-asset approaches. It emphasizes how allocation constraints, such as long-only requirements, leverage limits, and maximum exposure caps, impact optimal portfolio construction. The analysis shows that incorporating multiple asset classes yields greater diversification benefits, thereby enhancing risk-adjusted returns and improving retirement savings outcomes. Including real assets, such as private equity, private debt, real estate, and infrastructure, is valuable due to their unique risk-return profiles and lower correlations with traditional public equities and bonds. The framework acknowledges the practical challenges posed by liquidity risk and transaction costs, recognizing that real assets typically operate in markets with investment frictions during ramp-up and run-off phases when capital is deployed or withdrawn. It incorporates a time-varying liquidity weight that adjusts the portfolio's exposure to illiquid assets dynamically over the investment horizon. This mechanism reflects the natural lifecycle of investments. Younger investors can tolerate more illiquid investments for their potentially higher returns, while those approaching retirement gradually shift toward more liquid assets to ensure accessibility when needed.

Recognizing that inflation risk is a critical concern for retirement planning since inflation erodes the real purchasing power of accumulated wealth, the framework explicitly incorporates inflation dynamics and inflation-sensitive assets. By modeling inflation as a stochastic process and introducing assets whose returns are linked to inflation, the optimal allocation naturally decomposes into two components: a growth-oriented market portfolio and a liability-hedging portfolio designed to protect against inflation risk. This decomposition aligns defined contribution strategies with liability-driven investment principles used by defined benefit plans, ensuring that portfolios grow nominal wealth and preserve real value over time. From this perspective, assets serve as performance drivers and hedges against inflation risk. This underscores the importance of including inflation-sensitive assets, such as real assets.

detail.abstract: We show that banks' deposit market power originates from depositor inattention. Using transaction-level data on millions of U.S. depositors, we find that income with unknown timing stays in bank accounts about twice as long as paychecks with known timing. We measure depositor inattention as the gap in response times between unscheduled and scheduled income, and document that inattention dampens depositors' sensitivity to changes in deposit spreads. We scale this measure population-wide by modeling it as a function of demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Guided by these findings, we develop a theory where banks balance higher spreads against spread-sensitive outflows from inattentive depositors. The theory predicts, and the data confirm, that banks with more inattentive depositors set lower rates and pass through policy-rate changes less. Further, we estimate deposit flow sensitivity with a new leave-one-out instrument based on geographic inattention variation. Leveraging these empirical estimates, we calibrate banks' deposit franchise value and clarify how digital banking and monetary policy affect bank funding.

keywords: major questions doctrine JEL Classifications: F13

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the Trump administration's 2025 "reciprocal tariffs," imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) after a declaration of national emergency tied to U.S. trade deficits. We assess both the economic rationale and the legal implications of using IEEPA to raise U.S. tariffs and abandon Most Favored Nation (MFN) treatment. The Executive Order's claims-that trade deficits have surged, result from a lack of reciprocity, and have caused an "emergency" in manufacturing-rest on economic fallacies. Merchandise trade deficits are long-standing and largely endogenous; tariffs based on bilateral imbalances neither correct unfair foreign practices nor address any true emergency, let alone an 'unusual and extraordinary threat' as required by the statute. We further argue that the tariffs fail IEEPA's requirement that emergency measures "deal with" the asserted threat and that Congress never intended IEEPA to delegate sweeping tariff powers. The episode illustrates the perils of "commandeering the customs" through emergency powers to pursue trade policy by executive fiat.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel econometric framework for financial market forecasting that integrates market capitalization, volatility, trading volume, and newsdriven shocks into a unified predictive model. detail.abstract: This article examines the use of trademarks as domain names, meta tags, and keywords under Turkish law, focusing on Article 7(3)(d) of the Industrial Property Code No. 6769 (SMK), which expressly brings internet uses within the scope of infringement where the use has commercial effect and the user lacks a right or legitimate connection. Building on, and updating, my earlier German-language analysis (MarkenR 2011) to reflect the repeal of Decree-Law No. 556 and the enactment of the SMK, the paper maps the statutory framework, explains the conditions for unlawful use (commercial effect; absence of right/legitimate link), and differentiates among domain names, meta tags (“redirect codes”), and keyword advertising—three technically distinct modes that Turkish law regulates in a single clause. It contrasts Turkey’s explicit codification with the EU’s case-law-driven approach, and addresses special issues such as conflicts involving well-known marks, non-identical yet confusingly similar domain names, sectoral similarity, and the interface with unfair-competition rules. The analysis also considers comparative advertising limits under Turkish practice and their impact on keyword bidding. The paper concludes with practical enforcement guidance and a de lege ferenda suggestion that a mandatory cease-and-desist step precede litigation in internet-use disputes. Overall, it argues that SMK 7(3)(d) has clarified protection for online uses while leaving room for doctrinal refinement to better tailor remedies to the distinct technical contexts of domains, meta tags, and keywords.

detail.title: Complexity Theory and Economic Inequality
detail.abstract:
We analyze the potential for complexity theory to produce insights that elucidate the evolution of socioeconomic inequality and point toward effective policies. We position complexity theory as a complement to more traditional economic approaches. Economic models of inequality can fall into four broad categories: models based on individual attributes and technologies, social interaction models, intergenerational models of transfer, and models of institutional and social structure. Within each of these categories, complexity theory can enhance traditional theory. It is of particular value in helping to distinguish between bottom-up systemic and top-down structural causes of inequality. Complexity theory can further enrich our understanding of economic inequality by adopting a complex adaptive system of systems approach in which economic, social, political, and psychosocial systems interact with one another and with institutional and social structures to produce robust inequality, particularly on racial lines.

detail.title: Executive Expression: An Analysis of CEO Language and Gender in Earnings Calls
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether CEO gender is associated with differences in language in quarterly earnings calls, and how those differences (if any) correlate to short-term investor reaction. We collected Q1 2025 earnings call transcripts from 70 sector-and CEO gender-matched firms and measured CEO speech for hedge words and modal verbs using a Java-based text-processing code. We normalized frequencies for text length and conducted statistical tests. Results show no statistical differences between male and female CEOs in hedge word use (p = 0.3296) or modal verb use (p = 0.0790). Boxplots show substantial overlap between groups. Analysis of stock price reaction before and after earnings calls in comparable male-and female-led firms shows that male-led companies performed worse, but our study does not establish a causal relationship. These findings show language styles in high stakes communication to be similar for both sexes, and investor response may be reflective of more than language style.

detail.abstract: We examine the link between carbon intensity and US corporate bond spreads in a sample of disclosing companies before and after 2020. We find a consistent discount among high-intensity companies of approximately 11 bps prior to 2020 compared to companies with median carbon intensity. From 2020 to 2022, the discount increases to 16 basis points for A-rated bonds, while it turns insignificant for BBB-rated bonds. For A-rated bonds, we find an increasing term structure in the carbon discount. Our results imply a discrepancy between the carbon risk perception of bond market investors and credit rating agencies and a potential underpricing of climate risk. Our study contributes to the understanding of transition risks in industrial decarbonization by examining whether carbon intensity is priced in corporate bond markets, a key channel for financing industrial activities.

detail.title: Deteriorating Economy: The Negative Impact of the Intifadas on the Gaza Strip
detail.abstract: The Gazan economy has been on a trend of decline since the establishment of the state of Israel in 1948. This paper analyzes one of the most consequential periods in the Gazan economy, between the First and Second Intifadas (1987-2005), through a timeline analysis using per-capita economic indicators (GNI, GDP, and unemployment). By tracing developments from the First Intifada, through the Oslo Framework (Oslo I, Paris Protocol, and Oslo II), the post-Oslo economic shifts, the Camp David negotiations, and the Second Intifada, the paper demonstrates that Gaza's economic decline is not episodic, but rather structural. The region's economic framework has become dependent on external aid and on Israel, whose control over labor access and external border trade has limited Gaza's capacity for independent growth. This dependency has systematically ensured the persistence of financial crises within the Gazan economy and undermined any prospects for self-sufficiency.

detail.abstract:
The German statutory pension system faces structural challenges arising from demographic change, increasing life expectancy, and insufficient reserve mechanisms. This paper introduces the DARG Pension Model, an adaptive and system-theoretical reform framework that integrates both micro- and macro-level mechanisms into a mathematically closed system.

At the micro level, the model adjusts contributions and entitlements through dynamic contribution ceilings, demographic weighting, and biographical correction factors. These mechanisms account for income, wealth, family responsibilities, and years of employment, thereby strengthening fairness and reducing the risk of old-age poverty. At the macro level, automatic reserve accumulation and a demographically weighted pension value establish self-stabilizing feedback loops that mitigate demographic and economic shocks without requiring constant political intervention.

The formalized structure of the DARG Pension Model ensures internal consistency and allows transparent long-term simulations. The results demonstrate that a sustainable and equitable pension system is achievable when adaptive mechanisms replace ad hoc reforms, broadening the financial base while enhancing intergenerational stability. In doing so, the model directly addresses key challenges such as the looming financing gap, the growing risk of old-age poverty, and the impact of demographic change on pension sustainability.

detail.title: LLM Survey Framework: Coverage, Reasoning, Dynamics, Identification
detail.abstract:
We propose a new LLM-based survey framework that enables retrospective coverage, economic reasoning, dynamic effects, and clean identification. We recover human-comparable treatment effects in a multi-wave randomized controlled trial of inflation expectations surveys, at 1/1000 the cost. To demonstrate the framework’s full potential, we extend the benchmark human survey (10 waves, 2018–2023) to over 50 waves dating back to 1990. We further examine the economic mechanisms underlying agents’ expectation formation, identifying the mean-reversion and individual-attention channels. Finally, we trace dynamic treatment effects and demonstrate clean identification. Together, these innovations demonstrate that LLM surveys enable research designs unattainable with human surveys.

detail.abstract: Inflation in Switzerland has been low over the past 20 years, both from an international and a historical perspective. One hypothesis is that this is due to the high share of 'administered' - or regulated - prices in the Swiss consumer price basket. We show that this hypothesis is not supported by the data. Inflation for products with administered prices was typically lower than inflation for other products and thus tended to dampen inflation overall. However, the effect was limited. Swiss inflation and the Swiss inflation gap with the euro area were determined mainly by the evolution of non-administered prices.

detail.abstract:
In Don Quixote, there is a moment when all the knightly novels are thrown into the fire for their fantastical depictions of chivalry. Yet one book is spared: Tirant lo Blanc. It is saved because, unlike the others, it portrays knights who die in their beds-offering a more realistic depiction of medieval battles. Similarly, Liquid Asset stands out as the book that should be preserved from the extensive body of scholarship on water markets. Many works in this field are influenced by ideological biases that shape their analyses. In contrast, Buzz Thompson's books provides the nuance and balance often lacking in others.

Liquid Asset brings together key arguments from Professor Thompson's extensive scholarly work, weaving them into a cohesive and compelling narrative. While his contributions are too numerous to list in full, several stand out. First, the importance of institutional analysis, as explored in Institutional Perspectives on Water Policy and Markets. Second, the critical role of the private sector in protecting our resources and advancing societal goals, as examined in The Continuing Innovation of Citizen Enforcement. Third, the necessity of innovation in progressing toward sustainability, as discussed in The Path to Water Innovation.8 And fourth, the multifaceted nature of water as both an asset and a public good, as discussed in Water as a Public Commodity.

Liquid Asset delivers a clear and urgent message: addressing today's water challenges-and those to come-requires an all-hands-on- deck approach. This includes both the visible hand of government and the invisible hand of the private sector. The latter often not welcomed with open arms. However, successful collaboration demands adjustments to the water regulatory framework-both to accommodate and to place necessary limits on private sector involvement. I deliberately use the term "private sector" rather than "market," as Adam Smith's adage uses, because conflating all forms of private engagement in water under the singular concept of "market" is a mistake. Selling water rights, purchasing a public water utility, developing innovative water purification technologies, and conserving wetlands each require distinct analytical frameworks. Grouping them together risks alienating those who view markets as incompatible with water's inherently public nature-leading to the wholesale rejection of private sector participation.

The book is rich in data and comparative examples, offering infinite avenues for discussion. One particularly important issue it raises is the risk, or lack of it, of speculation in the robust model of water markets that it advocates.

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly capable of generating outputs that resemble human creativity, all without much human direction. This Article interrogates the frequent assertion among commentators, scholars, and policymakers that such AI-generated content is or will become a near-perfect substitute for human creative works. That assumption underpins widespread fears of AI displacing creative professions and undermining copyright law’s role in incentivizing human ingenuity. This Article challenges that narrative by identifying and analyzing foundational distinctions between artificial and human creativity—specifically, the absence in AI of intrinsic motivation, intentionality, and authenticity. These human-centric qualities are often essential to works that resonate emotionally and experientially with audiences, rendering human and AI outputs imperfect substitutes—and, in many cases, complements rather than competitors.

Drawing on literature in creativity studies, economics, and law, the Article establishes a framework for understanding when AI outputs are most likely to function as substitutes (e.g., in functional or utilitarian works) and when human creativity will retain market and cultural value (e.g., in expressive, emotionally resonant works). It then explores the implications of this analysis for copyright law. Contrary to some predictions, copyright remains essential in incentivizing human creative output, especially in collaborative environments where AI serves as a tool rather than an autonomous creator. The Article argues that copyright law is not facing obsolescence but rather a critical juncture requiring doctrinal adaptation. In particular, the Article evaluates pressing issues such as the copyrightability of AI-assisted works, the threshold for human authorship, and the growing influence of “market dilution” theories under copyright law’s fair use doctrine.

Ultimately, this Article offers a forward-looking vision in which copyright law continues to promote human creativity while evolving to accommodate a world where artificial and human forms of creativity increasingly intersect. Courts, the Copyright Office, and Congress must carefully distinguish between human and artificial contributions in shaping doctrine that balances innovation, legal coherence, and cultural values.

detail.title: Strategic Avoidance and the Welfare Impacts of U.S. Solar Panel Tariffs
detail.abstract:
This study examines the effects of tariffs imposed by the U.S. on imported solar panels. We first provide clear evidence that tariff-exposed firms shifted production to locations that did not face tariffs, and that domestic prices increased relative to other markets. We then develop a structural model to analyze welfare effects. We find that the tariffs generated modest gains for domestic manufacturers and for government revenues, but larger losses in domestic consumer surplus and environmental benefits, thereby reducing domestic welfare. Furthermore, the tariffs reduced domestic solar industry employment and wages. By contrast, subsidizing solar panel manufacturing could increase domestic production, employment, and welfare.

title: Different stakeholder-based forest management scenarios facilitate balancing conservation and production in the bioeconomy ​​

detail.title: Different stakeholder-based forest management scenarios facilitate balancing conservation and production in the bioeconomy ​​
detail.abstract: Land-use policies founded on the expertise and interests of key stakeholders are likely the most implementable and politically long-lasting, if a common perception about the future exists. We investigated whether there is a difference in how eleven indicator species of conservation concern may develop given policy and forestry scenarios of four key forest stakeholders for a 100,000 ha Swedish landscape over the coming 100 years. We used colonization-extinction models and species distribution models. Most species had stable or increasing metapopulation sizes or occurrence probabilities after 100 years under all except the most production-oriented scenario by private landowners. For six wood-decaying fungi, forests protected or managed with continuous cover forestry (CCF) drove the positive developments. By contrast, these species essentially disappeared from stands with even-aged clearcutting forestry. The 14.5% of forest with strict protection applied by the state-owned forest company increased the area occupied by these species. Protecting an even larger area and application of CCF in the scenarios of the (non-)governmental conservation organizations increased fungal metapopulation sizes even more. Four bird species showed stable or positive developments in all scenarios. The same held true for the epiphytic lichen Lobaria pulmonaria, because the management applied projected increasing host tree numbers and densities. Thus, protecting up to 20% of the productive forest, applying more alternative management regimes and less even-aged clearcutting rotation forestry has the potential to greatly increase the (meta)population size and improve the red-list status of the focal species, and presumably also of other species of conservation concern.

AI.method: 使用定殖-灭绝模型和物种分布模型，模拟四种关键森林利益相关者（私有土地所有者、国有林业公司、政府/非政府保护组织）的政策和林业情景对11种指示物种的影响。

detail.title: Monetary Policy and Housing Overvaluation
detail.abstract:
This paper examines how housing market overvaluation—measured by the price-to-rent ratio and its deviations from long-term trends—affects the transmission of monetary policy. Using U.S. metropolitan-level data and three measures of monetary policy shocks, we find that house prices respond more strongly to policy rate changes in overvalued markets. Examining buyer heterogeneity, we show that investor demand, proxied by non-owner-occupied purchases, declines more sharply after monetary tightening in these markets. These results are consistent with models of extrapolative beliefs and suggest that monetary policy can serve a stabilizing role during housing booms.
